preamble: Wordplay in each clue contains a superfluous letter to be ignored in reaching its solution. The solutions are to be fitted into the grid, jigsaw-wise, however they will go.

messages.text: CHANGE ONE LETTER TO MAKE PANGRAM

clue.text: ● Saw losers in favour of something that means action

indicators.note: read without its superfluous R as loses: the saw loses a part, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, a proverb
pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone saw the losers favour a particular course of action.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the R of 'losers', which really reads 'loses'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar books call a verb a doing word, the part of speech naming an action.

clue.text: ● Endearing lot get ejected from food plant

parts.note: read without its superfluous T as lo, the old word for look

indicators.note: something ejected is thrown out, so these letters leave the longer word

parts.note: a vegetable is a plant grown for food
taken as written

explanation.surface: A charming bunch are thrown out of a vegetable garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the T of 'lot', which really reads 'lo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endearing inspires affection, which is the same as being easy to love.

clue.text: ● Stimulate moderate politician to open hospital

indicators.note: read without its superfluous O as to pen: the politician pens, or encloses, the hospital letter

parts.note: a wet is a moderate in the Conservative party, a term from the Thatcher years
H is the map and signpost abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A centrist MP is invited to declare a new hospital open.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the O of 'open', which really reads 'pen'. A wet was Thatcher's word for a soft Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet an appetite or interest is to sharpen and stimulate it.

clue.text: ● Wrongly maligned stoical prisoner stabs smashing chap?

indicators.note: the prisoner stabs into the jumbled word, so it sits inside it
read without its superfluous M as wrongly aligned: letters set out of line are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
con is short for convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A calm convict, falsely slandered, knifes someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the M of 'maligned', which really reads 'aligned'. The question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An iconoclast literally smashed religious images, so he is a smashing chap in the sense of a breaker of idols.

clue.text: ● Hot meal atypically being delivered cold

indicators.note: a speech is delivered, so the word is spoken and only its sound counts

parts.note: read without its superfluous A as hot meal typically: chilli con carne is a typical hot meal

explanation.surface: A hot takeaway turns up cold, which is not the usual way.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the first A of 'atypically', which really reads 'typically'; chilli the dish and the adjective for cold sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilly weather is unpleasantly cold, so the adjective is a plain synonym.

clue.text: ● Administration knew Conservative politician supervised church shelters

indicators.note: the outer letters shelter the new one, holding it inside them

parts.note: Michael Gove is a Conservative cabinet minister
to run a business is to supervise it
CE is the Church of England
read without its superfluous K as new, abbreviated N

explanation.surface: The government knew a Tory minister had overseen church refuges.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the K of 'knew', which really reads 'new'. Michael Gove is a long-serving British Conservative minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Governance is the act or system of governing, which is the work of an administration.

clue.text: The superfluous letters from the clues (in the normal order of their solutions as found in the grid) spell out a final instruction that must be followed before the entry is submitted for the prize. ● Novel on hope by writer chides racist

indicators.note: read without its superfluous C as hides: the outer letters hide the jumble within

parts.note: X is the times sign, as in four by three
Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen

indicators.note: a novel arrangement is a new one, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer's novel about hope scolds a bigot.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the C of 'chides', which really reads 'hides'. Dimensions such as six by four use X for 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophobia is fear or hatred of foreigners, close kin to racial prejudice.

clue.text: ● Attractive woman and boyfriend cease to try

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or admirer

indicators.note: read without its superfluous E as case to: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lovely woman and her partner give up trying.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the first E of 'cease', which really reads 'case'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty is a strikingly good-looking person, especially a woman.

clue.text: ● Sound of howl or scream?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read without the superfluous H as sound of owl: the cry an owl makes
second meaning: a scream is something hilarious

explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the H of 'howl', which really reads 'owl'.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl's call is its classic cry, and informally a very funny person or thing is a riot or a scream.

clue.text: ● Old boy avoided juvenile court and part of sentence

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: read without its superfluous A as voided: the words are emptied, keeping only their first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written, stripped to its first and last letters
taken as written, likewise stripped to its ends

explanation.surface: A former pupil escaped a youth court and served part of his sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the A of 'avoided', which really reads 'voided'. 'Sentence' looks like a prison term but is grammatical.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the object is the noun phrase acted on by the verb, one component of a sentence.

clue.text: ● Cancelled publication was first to abandon arena

indicators.note: the letter is abandoned, so it leaves the word for the publication

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
read without its superfluous N as area, abbreviated A
to lead a race is to be first

explanation.surface: A magazine that once topped the field is axed and leaves the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the N of 'arena', which really reads 'area'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cancelled contract or marriage is annulled, declared void and of no effect.

clue.text: ● Hedonistic city's about to host writer pursuing grail

indicators.note: the reversed word plays host, holding the other letters inside it
turned about means reversed, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the word with its S, read letter by letter
read without its superfluous G as rail, and a rail is a bar
the writer of a clue refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A pleasure-loving city is about to welcome an author questing for the Holy Grail.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the G of 'grail', which really reads 'rail'. Sybaris was an ancient Greek city famous for luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybaritic means devoted to luxury and pleasure, like the citizens of Sybaris.

clue.text: ● Heightened awareness of speed limits is introduced by new model

indicators.note: the word forms the limits, its letters bounding the rest

parts.note: read without its superfluous P as seed

indicators.note: one piece is introduced by the others, so they come before it

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
to sit for an artist is to model
taken as written

explanation.surface: Speed restrictions are brought in by a new type of car, making drivers more alert.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the P of 'speed', which really reads 'seed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sensitise someone to an issue is to make them more conscious or alert to it.

clue.text: ● Paper out to launch dishonesty being relevant once more?

indicators.note: read without its superfluous A as out to lunch, slang for crazy, so the letters go haywire

parts.note: taken as written
lying is telling untruths

explanation.surface: A newspaper sets out to expose deceit, now topical again.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the A of 'launch', which really reads 'lunch'. The question mark covers a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule that is applying holds good or is relevant; doing so again is applying a second time.

clue.text: ● American conmen ultimately cheat crowds

indicators.note: the outer word crowds round the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: read without its superfluous E as chat, and to yak is to chat

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word

parts.note: only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: Swindlers eventually defraud the crowds in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the E of 'cheat', which really reads 'chat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is the informal British word for a person from the United States.

clue.text: ● Something in limbo can keep suffering

definitions.note: read without its superfluous O as something in limb, a part of the leg

indicators.note: letters that are suffering are in a bad way, knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soul in limbo goes on suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the O of 'limbo', which really reads 'limb'; it sits in the definition, not the wordplay as the preamble says.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap or patella is the bone at the front of the knee joint, part of the leg.

clue.text: ● Start off job when men supply boxes in plant

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter, taken off it

parts.note: only its first letter is used
as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: the jumbled letters box in the other one, holding it inside
supply in the sense of supple, flexible: the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
read without its superfluous N as i, the single letter I

explanation.surface: Begin work when the men provide window boxes of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the N of 'in', which really reads 'i'. 'Supply' here is an adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasmine is a climbing shrub with fragrant white or yellow flowers.

clue.text: ● Orders courts to support land in years to come

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: read without its superfluous N as lad in years to come: a boy grows into a man
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A judge orders the courts to back a land claim for future years.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the N of 'land', which really reads 'lad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official order or commission to act, so mandates are orders.

clue.text: ● Disconnect line bitten by gun dog

parts.note: read without its superfluous G as un, a dialect form of one

indicators.note: the line is bitten by the dog, held in its jaws

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A retriever trained to the gun bites through a cable.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the G of 'gun', which really reads 'un', as in 'a good un'. A gun dog retrieves shot game.
explanation.definitionFit: To unplug a device is to disconnect it by pulling its plug from the socket.

clue.text: ● Fellow overwhelmed by sources of torrent in full spate

definitions.note: read without its superfluous E as spat, a petty quarrel

indicators.note: the fellow is overwhelmed, swallowed up inside the other letters
the source of each word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A man is swept away by a river in full flood.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the E of 'spate', which really reads 'spat'; it sits in the definition, not the wordplay as the preamble says.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor squabble between friends or lovers, the same as a spat.

clue.text: ● Liberal country blocking adherent's dangerous flyer

indicators.note: the inner letters block the middle of the word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a fan is an adherent, the apostrophe S linking it to the rest
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
read without its superfluous R as county, abbreviated CO

explanation.surface: A Liberal-run country is threatened by a supporter's deadly aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the R of 'country', which really reads 'county'.
explanation.definitionFit: A falcon is a bird of prey, deadly to the smaller birds it hunts.

clue.text: ● Ruling state sent back English money in small change

definitions.note: read without its superfluous L as ruing state, a state of regret

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: pence are the small coins of British money

indicators.note: letters sent back travel the other way, read in reverse

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A governing nation returns English cash in coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the L of 'Ruling', which really reads 'Ruing'; it sits in the definition, not the wordplay as the preamble says.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitence is sorrow and regret for wrongdoing, a condition of ruing what one did.

clue.text: ● False idols going made place backward

indicators.note: read without its superfluous E as going mad: the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word is read backward, its letters reversed

parts.note: to lay something down is to place it

explanation.surface: Fake gods went mad and made a place regress.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the E of 'made', which really reads 'mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disloyal is false to a friend or cause, unfaithful in allegiance.

clue.text: ● Taxing backers of problem states is more sophisticated

indicators.note: read without its superfluous T as axing backers of: the back letter of each word is axed

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Taxing the sponsors of troubled countries is the smoother policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the T of 'Taxing', which really reads 'axing'. Change this S to Q, as the hidden instruction says, and the grid becomes a pangram.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave means smooth and urbane in manner, so the comparative means more polished or sophisticated.

clue.text: ● Action bureaucratic functionary's fiat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an action or ... at law, a lawsuit
second meaning: a ... is slang for an office bureaucrat in a business ...
third meaning, read without its superfluous A as fit: to fit

explanation.surface: An official's decree triggers a course of action.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the A of 'fiat', which really reads 'fit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit is a legal action, a suit is a faceless office type, and clothes that suit you fit you.

clue.text: ● Leaders of men are creating havoc for every individual

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: read without its superfluous M as en, a printer's measure; only its first letter is used
the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Ringleaders are causing chaos for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the M of 'men', which really reads 'en', a printer's measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Each is used adverbially, as in a pound each, meaning apiece or per person.

clue.text: ● Round figure concealed by outsize trousers

indicators.note: the figure is concealed by the words after it, its letters lying inside them

parts.note: its closing two letters
read without its superfluous T as rousers, whose opening two letters are used

explanation.surface: A rotund shape is hidden in baggy trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the T that opens 'trousers': drop it and the figure runs straight across outsiZE ROusers.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is written as a circle, the round figure, and also means nought.

clue.text: ● Thoughtlessness of niece regularly wearing revealing clothing

indicators.note: the clothing is worn by the letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: a negligee is a flimsy, often see-through dressing gown

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: read without its superfluous E as nice

explanation.surface: A niece is careless enough to go out in see-through clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The superfluous letter is the first E of 'niece', which really reads 'nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligence is failure to take proper care, a careless lack of attention.
